questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding the relationship between GDP, NDP, GNP and National Income:

Statement I: GDP is converted into GNP by adding Net Factor Income from Abroad.

Statement II: GNP is converted into NNP by deducting depreciation.

Statement III: NNP at Factor Cost is conventionally referred to as National Income.
questions.subject: Finance
questions.explanation: Correct option is D. Review the related concept in your syllabus notes.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding interdependence among sectors:

Statement I: Agriculture can provide raw materials required by certain manufacturing industries.

Statement II: Manufacturing may supply machinery and inputs required by agriculture.

Statement III: The tertiary sector can facilitate the movement, financing, and marketing of goods produced by the other sectors.
questions.subject: Finance
questions.explanation: Correct option is D. Review the related concept in your syllabus notes.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding disposable income:

Statement I: Personal Disposable Income is broadly the income available to households for consumption and saving after personal direct taxes.

Statement II: An increase in personal direct taxes, other things remaining constant, tends to reduce disposable income.

Statement III: Disposable income can never be saved because it must be entirely consumed.
questions.subject: Finance
questions.explanation: Correct option is A. Review the related concept in your syllabus notes.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding the overall structure of an economy:

Statement I: Primary, secondary, and tertiary sectors are interconnected rather than completely independent.

Statement II: Economic development can involve changes in the relative importance of all three sectors.

Statement III: A developed economy can have a tertiary sector without having any dependence on primary or secondary sector activities.
questions.subject: Finance
questions.explanation: Correct option is A. Review the related concept in your syllabus notes.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements:

Statement I: A fall in the price of a normal good generally increases its quantity demanded, ceteris paribus.

Statement II: This movement along the demand curve is called an increase in demand.

Which of the following is correct?

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct, but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect, but Statement II is correct.

questions.subject: Finance
questions.explanation: Correct option is C. Review the related concept in your syllabus notes.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding Selective Credit Control:

Statement I: Selective credit controls can be directed toward particular sectors or uses of credit.

Statement II: They differ from general quantitative measures that affect overall credit conditions.

Statement III: Selective credit control means that the RBI completely eliminates all credit creation by commercial banks.
questions.subject: Finance
questions.explanation: Correct option is A. Review the related concept in your syllabus notes.

questions.question:

Statement I: OMO involves the purchase or sale of government securities by the central bank.

Statement II: Purchase of securities by the RBI can inject liquidity into the banking system.

Statement III: Sale of securities by the RBI can potentially absorb liquidity from the banking system.
questions.subject: Finance
questions.explanation: Correct option is D. Review the related concept in your syllabus notes.

Statement I: Domestic income is related to factor incomes generated within the domestic territory.

Statement III: Domestic income necessarily includes all factor income earned by residents from abroad.
questions.subject: Finance

questions.question:
Regarding opportunity cost, consider the following:

Statement I: Opportunity cost represents the value of the next best alternative forgone.

Statement II: Opportunity cost is always measured in monetary terms.

Statement III: Opportunity cost arises because resources have alternative uses.
questions.subject: Finance
questions.explanation: Opportunity cost is the value of the next best alternative forgone.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding indirect taxes:

Statement I: GST is an example of an indirect tax.

Statement II: Indirect taxes are generally imposed on goods and services rather than directly on the income of individuals.

Statement III: An indirect tax can never influence the market price paid by consumers.
questions.subject: Finance
questions.explanation: GST in India is destination-based — tax accrues where goods/services are consumed.

questions.question:

Statement I: A rightward shift in the demand curve indicates an increase in demand at every relevant price.

Statement II: A movement upward along the same demand curve represents an increase in demand.

Which of the following is correct?

Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct, but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect, but Statement II is correct.

questions.question:
Regarding economic choice, consider:

Statement I: Choosing one alternative necessarily involves foregoing at least one other alternative when resources are scarce.

Statement II: Opportunity cost exists even when the chosen alternative has no explicit monetary price.

Statement III: Unlimited resources would make the problem of economic choice more severe.
questions.subject: Finance
questions.explanation: Opportunity cost is the value of the next best alternative forgone.
